While modern wallets following EIP-2 canonical signature rules produce low-s signatures, high-s signatures are technically valid ECDSA signatures. Crucially, any observer of a valid owner signature can derive a high-s counterpart by computing `s' = curve_order - s` — the recovered address is identical, making this a constructable input against any live wallet.

The recovered address is identical to the original signer, so the signature appears legitimate until `tryRecover` rejects the high-s value. The adversary can then repeatedly submit griefing UserOps targeting any AtomWallet.
